title: Voltage-sensitive channels and gap junctions form rewritable dynamical memories

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Voltage-sensitive channels and gap junctions form rewritable dynamical memories

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because ion channels and gap junctions are themselves voltage-sensitive, a transient voltage state can trigger progressive depolarization or gap-junction closure, so non-neural bioelectric circuits readily form dynamical-system memories that store information and change computation without changing the channel or junction hardware.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Non-neural Bioelectricity: What Bodies Think About

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The fact that a transient voltage state passing through a cell can set off a cycle of progressive depolarization (like an action potential) or gap junctional (GJ) closure means that such circuits readily form dynamical systems memories which can store different information and change their computational behavior without changing the hardware

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Non-neural Bioelectricity: What Bodies Think About”. Scope: Non-neural cell networks coupled by voltage-gated channels and gap junctions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-21: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Persistent state and computation changes are precise dynamical properties that public models can test. Existing resources establish feasibility and selected instances, but the general biological prevalence of such memories remains only partially resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Construct or reuse conductance models with voltage-sensitive channels and junctions, apply transient inputs, and test for multiple persistent attractors and altered input-output behavior with unchanged parameters.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Biophysical parameters for many non-neural networks are sparse.

Model attractors do not show that living non-neural tissues use them as memory.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Voltage-gated channel and connexin kinetics are public, and published ODE models can be re-run to see whether a transient voltage leaves a stable state. That tests the biophysical implication in models. It does not cover non-neural tissues generally, and tissue experiments that would separate dynamical memory from a changed proteome are not in one open dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate a transient voltage pulse with published channel and connexin gating and test for two stable voltages or coupling states; dynamical memory holds if the post-pulse state remains after the pulse and changes later input-output behavior with the same hardware.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Most kinetic parameters come from neurons or heterologous cells, not the non-neural tissues in the claim.

A persistent voltage in real tissue can be transcriptional or ultrastructural rather than a dynamical-system memory of the same channels.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.6
